outcome: Type of delivery (vaginal, emergency cesarean, planned cesarean)
cohort: 6,736 women aged 12 to 49 years who gave birth in Mexico between 2006 and 2012
finding: Different socio-demographic and obstetric factors were associated with different types of delivery.
mod_finding: Vaginal delivery was more common among indigenous women, those receiving care through public providers, and those with two or more children, while planned cesarean deliveries were associated with higher socioeconomic level, more years of schooling, and older age.
